secondary_keywords: what is a squad in agile
what is a tribe in agile
does spotify still use the spotify model
search_intent: Definition/methodology, with a secondary 'should we copy it and how' implementation intent
h1: Spotify Model: Squads, Tribes, Chapters and Guilds Explained
seo_title: Spotify Model: Squads, Tribes, Chapters and Guilds Explained
meta_description: The Spotify model explained: squads, tribes, chapters and guilds, who decides what, a worked reorganisation example, the criticism, and how to adapt it.
excerpt: Squads, tribes, chapters and guilds explained: what each unit is, who decides what, a worked reorganisation with chapter-lead load calculations, the criticism from Spotify insiders, and how the model compares with SAFe, LeSS and Scrum@Scale.
learning_objectives: Define squads, tribes, chapters and guilds and distinguish chapter from guild and squad from tribe
Explain the delivery-weighted matrix and who decides what
Distinguish what the 2012 paper says from later additions (trio, alliance) and from criticism
Design squads and chapters for an organisation and estimate a chapter lead's management load
Decide whether the Spotify model, SAFe, LeSS or Scrum@Scale fits a given situation
related_npi_course: Wayfinder: Leadership and Stakeholder Communication (named only in the page's existing PMAI box; not mentioned in the body)

external_references.title: Kniberg & Ivarsson, Scaling Agile @ Spotify with Tribes, Squads, Chapters & Guilds (October 2012), holub.com mirror
external_references.what_it_supports: Definitions of all four units; mini-startup; sit together; PO and agile coach; no formal squad leader; tribe as incubator under ~100 (Dunbar); chapter lead as line manager working in a squad; guild coordinator; matrix weighted towards delivery; professor and entrepreneur; system owner (<1/10 of time) and chief architect; dependency reports; Scrum of Scrums on demand; ~10% hack time; growth 30 to 250; 30+ teams in 3 cities; introduced gradually over the past year; journey in progress

external_references.title: Kniberg, Spotify engineering culture (part 1), Spotify Engineering blog, 27 March 2014
external_references.what_it_supports: Existence and date of the 2014 video series on Spotify's engineering blog (video content itself not transcribed or quoted)

external_references.title: Kniberg, No, I didn't invent the Spotify model (6 June 2015), Goodreads mirror of author blog
external_references.what_it_supports: 'wasn't actually intended to be a generic framework'; 'just the messenger'; companies adapting it not worse off, some improved

external_references.title: Linders, InfoQ: No Spotify model (6 October 2016)
external_references.what_it_supports: Marcin Floryan (Spotify chapter lead) talk at Spark the Change London 2016: model a simplified description, not to be copied

external_references.title: Jeremiah Lee, Spotify's Failed #SquadGoals (19 April 2020)
external_references.what_it_supports: 'only ever aspirational'; never fully implemented; matrix friction; autonomy without alignment; citing Joakim Sundén that alignment/accountability parts were never completed

external_references.title: Atlassian, Discover the Spotify model
external_references.what_it_supports: Squad 6–12, tribe 40–150, trio and alliance as later additions

external_references.title: The Scrum Guide (November 2020)
external_references.what_it_supports: Scrum Team typically 10 or fewer; cross-functional and self-managing ('who does what, when, and how')
